items.stem: A team changes only React component JavaScript and some styling, with no new native dependency. Which delivery path is appropriate?

options.text: Ship it as an EAS Update over the air to the existing build
options.rationale: Correct: pure JavaScript and asset changes within the same runtime version can ship over the air without a new store build.

options.text: Submit a brand-new build to both app stores and wait for review
options.rationale: A full store submission is unnecessary when no native code or runtime version changed.

options.text: Bump the native runtime version and rebuild
options.rationale: The runtime version only changes when the native layer changes; it did not here.

options.text: Nothing can be delivered without Xcode on a local machine
options.rationale: EAS builds in the cloud and OTA updates need no local native toolchain.

items.explanation: Correct: pure JavaScript and asset changes within the same runtime version can ship over the air without a new store build.

items.stem: Which TWO changes CANNOT be delivered through an EAS Update over the air and require a new native build? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Adding a new native module that needs native code
options.rationale: Correct: new native code is compiled into the binary and cannot ship over the air.

options.text: Changing the app's minimum supported OS, which alters the native build
options.rationale: Correct: native build configuration changes require a rebuilt binary.

options.text: Editing the text of an on-screen label
options.rationale: Text changes are JavaScript and can ship over the air.
Style changes are JavaScript and can ship over the air.

items.explanation: Correct: new native code is compiled into the binary and cannot ship over the air.

items.stem: A production OTA update introduces a crash. What is the fastest safe response using EAS Update?

options.text: Republish the previous known-good update to the production branch
options.rationale: Correct: republishing the last good update rolls clients back without a store review.

options.text: Submit a new build and wait for store review
options.rationale: Store review is slow and unnecessary when a prior good JavaScript bundle exists.

options.text: Delete the app from the stores
options.rationale: Removing the app harms all users and does not fix the update.
Users cannot be relied on to reinstall and it does not address the bad bundle.

items.explanation: Correct: republishing the last good update rolls clients back without a store review.
